summary: The visual-structure-discovery lane is sound enough as a discovery-only sidecar for WCAG 1.3.1 / 2.4.6 and optional AAA 2.4.10 follow-up, but required hardening so discovery evidence cannot look like a definite barrier and prompt packets actually include visual evidence.

findings.risk: Discovery verdict was prompt-enforced, not code-enforced
findings.remediation: Discovery-only aspects are now clamped in broad-scope LLM review: reveal-state-discovery and visual-structure-discovery always reconcile to UNCERTAIN even if judge and critic agree on LIKELY_BARRIER.

findings.risk: Prompt pack was stale relative to visual evidence
findings.remediation: Prompt artifacts were regenerated after screenshot capture; positive visual-structure packets now include visual refs and visualAgreement. The prompt-pack audit now fails if expected visual refs are missing.

findings.risk: Generated 10/10 coverage is useful but narrow
findings.remediation: Recorded as a limitation. Current positives cover non-semantic visual headings, bullet-like groups, and CSS grid tables; negatives cover semantic headings, lists, tables, and large control text. Future adversarial cases should add ARIA equivalents, CSS counters, flex tables, layout grids, responsive breakpoints, card-title false positives, and aria-hidden/inert variants.

findings.risk: SC scoping could imply 2.4.10 baseline conformance scope
findings.remediation: The aspect wording now labels 2.4.10 as optional AAA follow-up; sidecar packets remain non-authoritative and convert no v3 judgments.

remainingLimitations: The lane is heuristic discovery, not a complete visual structure algorithm.
It does not prove a WCAG failure by itself; LLM or downstream deterministic checks must judge whether the visual grouping is meaningful and whether programmatic relationships are required.
It currently covers generated visible HTML/CSS structures only, not full-page tiled OCR, canvas/SVG text, below-fold pressure on saved websites, responsive breakpoints, shadow DOM, or iframe content.
2.4.10 is an optional AAA follow-up and must not be interpreted as EN/WCAG A-AA baseline publication scope.
